clue.text: Order stationery for government document

parts.note: to order someone is to command them
writing paper is the commonest stationery

explanation.surface: Someone requisitions office supplies for an official report.
explanation.definitionFit: A Command Paper is a British government report formally presented to Parliament by royal command.

clue.text: Absurd behaviour by adult hard to correct in church

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit within the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: correcting something rearranges it, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grown-up's ridiculous conduct is hard to put right in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to correct' scrambles the adult letter with the word hard; 'in' places that mix inside the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence, a show that deceives no one.

clue.text: Makes fast ship for some Arabs

definitions.meaning: to tie up a vessel at a berth
North African Muslims of Arab and Berber descent

explanation.surface: A quick vessel being built for Arab sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: To moor is to secure a vessel; Moors were the Muslims of North Africa and medieval Spain.

clue.text: Stupidly I mangle books to get arrangement in a row

indicators.note: doing something stupidly means getting it jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A clumsy reader ruins their books while trying to shelve them in line.
explanation.definitionFit: Alignment is the placing of things in a straight line.

clue.text: Diarist reported national assembly

indicators.note: signals a word that sounds like the name spoken aloud

parts.note: Iain Dale is a British broadcaster whose blog was called Iain Dale's Diary

explanation.surface: A journal-writer gives an account of a parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: English speakers commonly pronounce the Irish word as 'dale', matching the diarist's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dáil is the lower house of Ireland's parliament.

clue.text: Unusual sailor needs constellation with luminance

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
Norma is a small southern constellation, the Carpenter's Square
L is the physics symbol for luminance

explanation.surface: An odd sailor wants stars and light.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnormal means departing from the usual or typical.

clue.text: Defeated but not at first worried

indicators.note: the opening letter of the synonym is removed

parts.note: beaten means defeated

explanation.surface: Someone was beaten but only worried later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defeated' looks like the definition, but it loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaten up, consumed by anxiety: eaten here means troubled or gnawed at.

clue.text: Arc-en-ciel formed without a surround

indicators.note: the letters are formed into a new word, so they are rearranged
says the letter a is left out of the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: A French rainbow shaped with no ring around it.
explanation.walkthrough: Arc-en-ciel is French for rainbow; drop A and rearrange RCENCIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To encircle is to form a ring round, to surround.

clue.text: Person getting diamond waistcoat

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a jewelled waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is a close-fitting upper garment, in older usage a waistcoat or corset.

clue.text: End gift after a literary one gets in

indicators.note: the literary-one pair goes inside the word for gift

parts.note: a boon is a gift or blessing
LIT is the standard abbreviation for literary
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A writer's present seems to bring something to a close once it is admitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the gift behind A; 'gets in' puts LITI inside BOON.
explanation.definitionFit: Abolition is the formal ending or doing away with something, as of slavery.

clue.text: Dance's beat and energy

definitions.note: read as 'Dance is', the 's linking definition to wordplay

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A dance described as all rhythm and vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance originating in Argentina.

clue.text: Accede when told to go

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'
someone sent away has been told to go

explanation.surface: Someone gives in at the moment they are ordered to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when told' tempts a homophone of ascent, but no sound device is at work: the words simply split in two.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to agree or give consent, the same as acceding to a request.

clue.text: Bishop, outside, is starting to imbibe port

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
rind is the outer skin of fruit or cheese
taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A bishop drinks port outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink but is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Brindisi is a seaport on the heel of Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Eastern concoction of prime compound

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters of the next word are mixed up

explanation.surface: An Oriental brew made from the best ingredients.
explanation.definitionFit: An epimer is a chemical compound, an isomer differing at one asymmetric carbon atom.

clue.text: Libeling criminal in poor health

indicators.note: something criminal is wrong or crooked, so these letters are twisted

explanation.surface: Slander that is criminal leaves its victim unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-being is the opposite of wellbeing: a state of sickness or unhappiness.

clue.text: Non-metrical hymn may amuse, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the words are spoken aloud and a soundalike is entered

parts.note: something that may amuse can tickle you

explanation.surface: A hymn without regular metre could be amusing, people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A canticle is a hymn or chant with a biblical text, sung in church services rather than in metre.

clue.text: Twin adder struck a blow

indicators.note: struck means hit and knocked about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pair of snakes lashed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struck a blow' reads as one phrase; 'struck' is the anagram signal and 'a blow' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade wind is a steady wind, and a blow is a gust or gale.

clue.text: Slick Ron cut smooth tuft from maize

indicators.note: something cut is chopped up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Ron trims a sleek tuft off a corn cob.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn silk is the glossy threads of style that sprout from an ear of maize.

clue.text: As an example my cousin kicked Oriental

indicators.note: something kicked about is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cousin of mine lashed out at someone from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my cousin' is the example, so the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is one example of a family member or kinsman.

clue.text: Genuine manuscript provides fields for study

parts.note: real means genuine

explanation.surface: An authentic manuscript opens up areas of research.
explanation.definitionFit: Realms are domains or spheres of knowledge.

clue.text: Carved pieces of jewellery turned out bone

parts.note: came, as in 'it came about', means turned out or happened
OS is Latin for bone, used in anatomy

explanation.surface: Carved jewels are revealed to be made of bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameos are small carved reliefs, typically on shell or stone, worn as brooches.

clue.text: Purees whisked with a hint of vanilla and put on the table

indicators.note: whisked means beaten up, so these letters are mixed
just the first letter of the flavouring is used

explanation.surface: Fruit purees are whipped up with a dash of vanilla and served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hint of' gives V, which joins PUREES in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve up food is to dish it out and place it before diners.

clue.text: It's encouraging one gambling

parts.note: a means one
betting is gambling on an outcome

explanation.surface: It is good news when someone gambles, or so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Abetting is encouraging or assisting, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Some altos can be heard in this

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few alto singers can perform in this work.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is a Puccini opera, which singers, altos among them, are heard in.

clue.text: Magistrate's expression of surprise being put inside

definitions.note: read as 'Magistrate is', the 's linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: the word for being is placed within the exclamation

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
ens is the philosophical Latin term for being or existence

explanation.surface: A judge looks surprised at someone being sent to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being put inside' suggests imprisonment; 'being' is the philosophers' Latin term, and 'put inside' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome a censor was a magistrate who kept the census and oversaw public morals.

clue.text: Short Canadian in street

indicators.note: the Canadian abbreviation sits within the street abbreviation

parts.note: CAN is the abbreviation for Canadian

explanation.surface: A Canadian of small stature standing in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient, in short supply.

clue.text: Fatuous joke's Australian

parts.note: a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A silly joke told by an Aussie.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga means senile or foolishly infatuated, so silly.

clue.text: Diminished by its short linear representation

definitions.meaning: reduced by an amount, as in arithmetic subtraction
the subtraction sign is drawn as a short horizontal line

explanation.surface: A quantity reduced, and the little dash that shows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Minus means less by a given amount, and its sign is a brief dash.

clue.text: One northern bird brought back, chewed — dead

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the bird's name is turned round

parts.note: mina is a variant spelling of myna, an Asian starling
chewed food is food you ate

explanation.surface: A northern bird is returned, mauled and lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanimate means lifeless, without the signs of life.

clue.text: Short retreat from cryptic domestic animals

parts.note: domestic animals are pets, and the word step written backwards spells pets

explanation.surface: Animals backing off a little from a puzzling household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' tells you to read the answer itself as wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A backward step is a small withdrawal, a brief move back.
